review: Independent follow-up of the three DCP1 hold findings

resolved_findings.evidence: Present SSE IDs must now be nonempty strings of at most 512 characters and are compared without truncation; changing IDs fail as protocol_error.
Empty, non-string, and over-512-character IDs fail closed; the real CLI synthetic transport includes non-string, oversized, and changing-ID cases.
Hardware note, trial note, and rationale consistently describe DCP1; the immutable publisher image tag's DCP2 name is explicitly explained and startup remains the effective-setting gate.

accepted_trial_envelope: Use the managed candidate recipe bound to registry digest cfbc4dc4f4f7e8a73590e21cf95e7586172aab67dc4a892a51ca45adc77607f4 and rendered recipe digest 561d548b4124a98493c88c4145405f40ed25c747bde9ddf9a17696fe8a96661d.
Keep the candidate isolated at 127.0.0.1:8002 with no route, client-catalog, driver, image, weights, KV dtype, APC, batching, context, sequence cap, containment, or speculation change.

After managed load, require startup logs and managed identity to prove effective DCP1 and measure KV capacity. The measured capacity must exceed the actual tokenized simultaneous prompt plus maximum-output demand before the 175K/32K request.
Run the one-round small thinking-enabled overlap scenario first, then the one-round 175K/32K overlap only if small runtime, retrieval, token, identity, and coverage gates pass.
Stop immediately on Xid, CUDA error, engine death, OOM, identity drift, missed coverage, malformed/server error, or unrelated workload; preserve native, owner, kernel, status, and identity evidence.
A passing arm is bounded mitigation evidence only. It does not establish kernel root cause, crash rate, full C4 context capacity, performance eligibility, qualification, or promotion.
Restore and verify the exact DCP2 baseline afterward. Do not deliberately rerun the known-crashing parent overlap merely to satisfy reverse-order control guidance.
